questions.questionText: Magnetic susceptibility of a diamagnetic material is:
questions.solution: Diamagnetic: small negative susceptibility.

questions.questionText: Curie's law applies to:
questions.solution: Curie's law chi = C/T applies to paramagnets.

questions.questionText: Magnetic field lines of a bar magnet form:
questions.solution: Magnetic field lines always form closed loops.

questions.questionText: Above the Curie temperature a ferromagnet becomes:
questions.solution: Thermal agitation destroys domain alignment making it paramagnetic.

questions.questionText: Relative permeability of a diamagnetic material is:
questions.solution: For diamagnetic materials mu_r is slightly less than 1.

questions.questionText: An example of a ferromagnetic material is:
questions.solution: Iron is a classic ferromagnet.

questions.questionText: Magnetic declination at a place is the angle between:
questions.solution: Declination is the angle between geographic and magnetic meridians.

questions.questionText: The angle of dip at the magnetic equator is:
questions.solution: At magnetic equator field is horizontal so dip = 0.

questions.questionText: The angle of dip at the magnetic poles is:
questions.solution: At poles field is vertical so dip = 90 degrees.

questions.questionText: Hysteresis loss is least in:
questions.solution: Soft iron has narrow hysteresis loop giving least loss.

questions.questionText: Permanent magnets are made from:
questions.solution: Steel retains magnetization - good for permanent magnets.

questions.questionText: The relation B = mu0(H + M) connects:
questions.solution: B = mu0(H + M) relates magnetic flux density B, field intensity H, and magnetization M.

questions.questionText: Total earth's field with horizontal H and vertical V component is:
questions.solution: B = sqrt(H^2 + V^2) since they are perpendicular.

questions.questionText: Susceptibility of a paramagnetic material is:
questions.solution: Paramagnetic materials have small positive susceptibility.

questions.questionText: A magnetic dipole in a uniform field experiences:
questions.solution: Uniform field: torque but no net force on a dipole.

questions.questionText: Domain theory explains behaviour of:
questions.solution: Magnetic domain theory explains ferromagnetism.

questions.questionText: If dip angle is delta and horizontal component is H, vertical component V is:
questions.solution: tan(delta) = V/H so V = H tan(delta).

questions.questionText: Electromagnets use soft iron because:
questions.solution: Soft iron has low coercivity - easy to magnetize/demagnetize.

questions.questionText: Gauss's law for magnetism states:
questions.optionA: Flux integral of B over closed surface = mu0*I
questions.optionB: Flux integral of B over closed surface = 0
questions.optionC: Flux integral of E over closed surface = 0
questions.solution: Net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero (no monopoles).

questions.questionText: Magnetization M is defined as:
questions.solution: M = magnetic moment per unit volume.

questions.questionText: Diamagnetic substances are:
questions.solution: Diamagnets are weakly repelled by magnetic fields.

questions.questionText: Field inside a paramagnetic material compared to applied field is:
questions.solution: Paramagnets slightly enhance the field (mu_r > 1).

questions.questionText: The unit of magnetic pole strength is:
questions.solution: Pole strength unit is A*m.

questions.questionText: Retentivity is:
questions.optionA: Magnetization retained after removing external field
questions.solution: Retentivity is the residual magnetization when external field becomes zero.

questions.questionText: Coercivity is:
questions.optionB: Reverse field needed to reduce M to zero
questions.solution: Coercivity is the reverse H needed to demagnetize the material.
